A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MaxSup study, with 27 readable pages including Appendices A–L. Full text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the scientific content, figures, tables and proofs.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, transfer, robustness and segmentation experiments, including ImageNet results in Table 4, ADE20K results in Table 9 and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the classification and segmentation evaluations in Tables 4 and 9 and the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The MaxSup objective, top-1-logit penalty and training procedure are identical in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions retain identical ImageNet and CIFAR evaluations, fine-grained and long-tailed classification, CIFAR-10-C corruption testing, ADE20K segmentation and Appendix G transfer datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator sets. This includes OLS and Zipf-LS, the long-tailed Focal Loss comparisons, and Appendix H's Confidence Penalty, Adaptive Label Smoothing and Logit Normalization comparisons.

E3.justification: Training recipes, model configurations, augmentation settings, evaluation metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. Section 4.2.1 and the appendices retain the same training schedules, imbalance ratios and linear-transfer hyperparameter searches.

E4.justification: The LS-component ablation, corruption evaluation, training-recipe and weight-schedule tests, Grad-CAM examples, feature-space analyses and logit visualizations are identical, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting is unchanged, including Tables 4, 5, 10 and 13. Table 8 retains its mean(std) reporting across three setups; no run information or statistical procedure is revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–16 and Figures 1–5 retain identical results. For example, Table 4 reports ImageNet ResNet-50 accuracy of 77.69 ± 0.07% for MaxSup and 76.91 ± 0.11% for Label Smoothing in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 3's definitions, loss decomposition and gradients are unchanged. Appendices A–C retain identical proofs and derivations, including the treatment of CutMix and Mixup.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion make identical claims about LS error amplification, MaxSup's preservation of intra-class variation and its classification and transfer benefits.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including the minority-class limitation and the conclusion's open questions about distillation, training dynamics and interactions with weight regularization.

D1.justification: Reported code links, implementation instructions, training hyperparameters, pseudocode and computational timing information are identical. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 49 reference entries are unchanged. Apparent bibliography differences disappear when entries are matched across the shifted page breaks.

P1.justification: v4 adds Meta AI and Max Planck Institute affiliations, expands author footnotes, and revises acknowledgments to include DFG L2S and EU ELSA funding and an EU disclaimer. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The front-page affiliation and footnote blocks change, and longer acknowledgments reflow the bibliography across pages 11–14. All scientific figures, tables and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added affiliations and funding disclosures improve attribution completeness, but the scientific exposition, methods, theory, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information are identical. These administrative clarifications and minor layout shifts do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
